children: Swiss drugmaker Roche has entered a licensing deal with China's Simcere Pharmaceutical for the development of a blood cancer drug.

Roche will pay $75.0 million upfront for the exclusive global rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize SIM0660, an antibody targeting B-cell malignancies, Simcere said Tuesday. The drug could potentially treat blood cancers and some types of autoimmune diseases.
Simcere is also eligible for up to $1.455 billion in milestone payments, and tiered royalties on future net sales, it said.

The agreement is the latest tie-up between Western pharmaceutical majors and Chinese drugmakers. U.S.-based Bristol-Myers Squibb in May struck a strategic partnership and licensing deal with Hengrui Pharmaceuticals that could be worth more than $15 billion. Earlier this year, Eli Lilly entered into a partnership with Innovent Biologics potentially valued at up to $8.5 billion.
Shares of Simcere were 5.5% higher at 11.58 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to $1.48, early Wednesday.
